title: Training-crawler policy is stated
question: Has the site made a decision about AI training crawlers, whatever it is?
method: Pass when robots.txt states a training decision in any form: a group for the shared token __usage_ai-training (an IETF draft that Microsoft honours from 2027-02-01 and Google intends to honour from early 2027, with an explicit Google-Extended group taking precedence), groups naming the documented training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot, CCBot, Bytespider, MistralAI-Training), or a Content-Signal or Content-Usage line that sets ai-train or train-ai. Allowing and disallowing count the same: blocking training is a licensing decision and never loses points. Warn when nothing is stated or there is no robots.txt. That warning is this project's position that a decision should be explicit, not a vendor rule. The evidence lists the effective verdict per token.

title: Search and assistant crawlers may read product pages
question: Do the crawlers that feed AI answers get in?
method: Evaluate robots.txt against a sampled product path (the home page when none) for the crawlers that build the indexes behind AI answers: Googlebot and Bingbot (Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT search, whose results come from Microsoft's index, and Claude search via Brave), Applebot, Storebot-Google (Google's Shopping surfaces), OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot (a blocked page is reduced to domain, headline and a short summary), Amzn-SearchBot, DuckAssistBot, MistralAI-Index and meta-webindexer. Fail when Googlebot or Bingbot is disallowed or when two or more of the others are. Warn when exactly one is. Pass otherwise, including when there is no robots.txt. A warning still meets the Level 1 gate, because the crawlers behind the largest AI answer surfaces can read the page. The evidence shows the effective rule per crawler.

spec.title: OpenAI: searching the web with ChatGPT (search providers)

title: Usage-preference signals parse
question: Are the machine-readable usage preferences the site declares well-formed?
method: Informational. Collect every usage-preference signal found: Content-Signal lines in robots.txt, Content-Usage rules in robots.txt and the Content-Usage response header, an RSL License line in robots.txt or a Link header or <link> of type application/rsl+xml, and TDM reservations (/.well-known/tdmrep.json, the tdm-reservation and tdm-policy headers or meta tags). Pass when every signal present is syntactically valid. Warn when one is malformed. Not applicable when none is declared, since declaring none is a valid choice. The three vocabularies share no tokens and are never mapped onto each other, and no crawler operator documents honouring Content-Signal, so this is reported and never scored.

title: No block or challenge on an honest fetch
question: Does an agent that identifies itself truthfully get the pages?
method: Inspect the responses the scan made with its own user agent (AgenticReadinessScanner, with a documentation URL): the home page, robots.txt, the sampled product pages and the same-origin policy pages. A page is blocked when it answered 401, 402, 403, 406, 429 or 451, carried a bot-management challenge marker (cf-mitigated or x-vercel-mitigated: challenge, a DataDome captcha, a small page with challenge wording) or was answered by an access-denied page served as 200. The message names the product behind it when the response does (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, Vercel, Imperva, HUMAN (PerimeterX), AWS WAF, Fastly). Fail when the home page, robots.txt or a product page is blocked: the store is unreachable for any agent that is not on an allow list. A home page that refuses the scanner still produces a report: this check fails, robots.txt and the sitemap are evaluated, and every check that needs the pages is marked not evaluated. Warn when a page redirected to a consent or geographic interstitial instead of its content. Pass with a note when only a policy page is refused (a login wall in front of a support form, a stricter rule on legal pages): the agent can browse and buy, and B4.6 reports that it cannot read that policy. A page that could not be fetched at all (a dropped connection) is reported as such and never counted as a block, and the check is skipped when no page could be fetched. The scanner never impersonates another agent, so what it meets is what any unverified agent meets. Crawlers verified by published IP ranges or signed requests may be let through, which the message says.

spec.title: Cloudflare: detecting a challenge page response

title: User-triggered fetchers are not disallowed
question: When a person asks an assistant about this site, may the assistant fetch the page?
method: Evaluate robots.txt against the sampled product path (the home page when none) for the fetchers assistants use at the moment a person asks: ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Agent, meta-externalfetcher, Amzn-User and MistralAI-User. Fail when any is disallowed, pass otherwise, including when there is no robots.txt. OpenAI, Perplexity, Meta and Amazon document that these fetch regardless of robots.txt because a person requested the page (Anthropic honours it, and Mistral does not say), so a Disallow mostly records intent. The weight is low for that reason.

title: No directives that keep product pages out of AI answers
question: Do the pages stay eligible for a snippet, which is what AI answers are built from?
method: Read the robots, googlebot, bingbot and applebot meta tags and the X-Robots-Tag header of each sampled product page. Fail on noindex, on nosnippet or max-snippet:0 (Google documents that these keep the content out of AI Overviews and AI Mode, and Apple generates no web answer from such a page), and when one data-nosnippet element wraps half or more of the page text. Warn on noarchive or nocache (Bing keeps the page out of Copilot answers or reduces it to URL, title and snippet until 2027-03-01, and Amazon reads noarchive as a training opt-out), on Bing's page-level ai-grounding:disallow or disallowextended (honoured from 2027-02-01 under the Bingbot name, and flagged wherever the scanner finds it), and on isAccessibleForFree:false (Apple does not use the page as AI context). Record noai and noimageai as declared preferences without a verdict, since no documented answer engine reads them. Not applicable when no product page was sampled.

title: Render resources not blocked by robots.txt
question: May the crawlers that render pages fetch the scripts and stylesheets the page needs?
method: Collect up to 50 same-origin script and stylesheet URLs of the sampled product pages (the home page when none were sampled) and evaluate each path against robots.txt for Googlebot and Bingbot. Fail when any is disallowed for Googlebot: Google does not render JavaScript from blocked files, Applebot follows Googlebot rules and cannot render with blocked resources, and Bing excludes content it cannot render from grounding. Warn when only Bingbot is blocked. Pass when nothing is blocked or there is no robots.txt. Cross-origin assets are outside this file and are not judged, and neither are scripts under cart, basket, bag, checkout, account, order or admin paths (and their German and French forms): platforms disallow those areas on purpose (Shopify ships a checkout preload script on every product page) and a product page renders without them. Not applicable when the page loads no same-origin scripts or stylesheets.

title: WordPress search engine visibility
question: Has the WordPress site asked search engines to stay away?
method: On a WordPress site (WooCommerce included), read the robots meta tag and the X-Robots-Tag header of the home page. Fail when either carries noindex (or none) for all crawlers, ignoring a header scoped to one crawler (bingbot: noindex). The message says whether it is the exact "noindex, nofollow" tag WordPress core prints when Settings > Reading > Search engine visibility is ticked, which also turns off the core sitemap. Pass otherwise. No extra request.

title: Squarespace AI crawler setting
question: Does Squarespace's AI crawler block shut out the crawlers behind AI answers?
method: On a Squarespace site, evaluate robots.txt at the root for the 26 user agents Squarespace documents for Settings > Crawlers > "Block known artificial intelligence crawlers". The setting is taken as on when at least 60% of them (16 of 26) are disallowed. Pass when it is off, or on but blocking only training crawlers. Warn when it is on and also disallows agents that feed AI answers (DuckAssistBot, YouBot). Blocking training crawlers is a licensing choice and never loses points. Not applicable when robots.txt could not be read. No extra request.

spec.title: Squarespace: Request that AI models exclude your site

title: Webflow traffic control
question: Has a Webflow Traffic control switch shut search engines or AI bots out?
method: On a Webflow site, evaluate robots.txt at the root for the two bot groups Webflow documents under Site settings > SEO > Indexing > Traffic control: search engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot and ten more) and AI bots (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, GPTBot and fifteen more). A group counts as switched off when at least 60% of it is disallowed (8 of 13 or 12 of 19). Fail when either group is off, because the search group feeds search and the AI answers built on it, and the AI group includes the fetchers that read pages for ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity answers. Pass when both are allowed, which is Webflow's default. Not applicable when robots.txt could not be read. No extra request.

spec.title: Webflow: Disable search engine indexing (Traffic control)

title: Square Online search visibility
question: Is the Square Online site hidden from search engines?
method: On a Square Online site, read the home page's robots meta tag and X-Robots-Tag header (ignoring a header scoped to one crawler) and the robots.txt rules for Googlebot and Bingbot. Fail when the home page carries noindex (or none) or robots.txt disallows both crawlers at the root, which is what Square's "Hidden from search engine results" setting asks for. Pass otherwise. Search indexes feed the AI answers built on them. No extra request.

title: Salesforce robots.txt not on the staging preset
question: Has a Salesforce Commerce Cloud storefront kept the robots.txt meant for staging instances?
method: On a Salesforce B2C Commerce storefront, evaluate robots.txt. Fail when it disallows Googlebot and Bingbot everywhere, which is what the Business Manager option "All Spiders Disallowed to Access Any Static Resources" for development and staging instances produces (robots.txt is a site preference and is replicated from staging to production), or when it disallows /on/demandware.static/, where SFRA storefronts serve their scripts, styles and images. Pass otherwise. No extra request.
